brief: The AI selloff has crushed US AI hardware names while Chinese AI-compute competitors held up, a divergence TS Lombard reads as the start of China becoming the world's low-cost compute supplier, comparable to its past dominance of solar and batteries. Evidence: China's semiconductor ETF (3191 HK) has outperformed the SOX over the past month; Nvidia's share of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026 as Huawei rose to 28%, with US export restrictions accelerating China's domestic substitution rather than blocking it. China's edge compounds through power: it added roughly 10x US generating capacity in 2025, and Inner Mongolia data centers pay about half the US industrial electricity rate, so compute demand could migrate to the cheapest power as Chinese competitors scale. Because open-weight models (72% of OpenRouter tokens, 27% of spending, 69% from Chinese labs) make compute increasingly interchangeable, value shifts to distribution and cheap supply, pressuring Nvidia's roughly 75% gross margin the way Chinese scale cut solar and battery prices 95% and 90%. The thesis: not weaker Western AI demand, but structurally lower margins. The note floats low-delta upside calls on SMHC, down roughly half from its summer highs, to express it.
